records.statement: User story US-01: As the content operator, I want to create a content project in a web interface by selecting a competition, season and matchday, so that the platform prepares coverage of that matchday.

User story US-02: As the content operator, I want the platform to research the selected matchday (results, teams and scores, dates, standings and competition context) and to show me the progress of the research, so that I receive structured, source-attributed data without collecting it by hand.

User story US-03: As the content operator, I want every fact to be verified independently against reliable sources and marked as verified or not verified, so that content with invented or unverified scores, standings or statistics cannot be approved.

User story US-04: As the content operator, I want the platform to draft the carousel structure, headlines, slide descriptions, social media caption and hashtags from the verified data, so that I start my review from a complete draft.

User story US-05: As the content operator, I want cover, match-result, standings and closing slides generated in the El Deporte Rey GT visual identity from reusable templates, so that every post looks professional and consistent.

User story US-06: As the content operator, I want an automated visual quality check of every slide before my review, so that wrong scores, standings or team names, overflowing text, inconsistent visuals and wrong dimensions are caught.

User story US-07: As the content operator, I want to preview the carousel and captions, regenerate individual slides and explicitly approve the content, so that nothing I have not approved can be exported.
User story US-08: As the content operator, I want to export the approved images and captions, so that I can publish them manually on Instagram.

User story US-09: As the content operator, I want a history of generated content with traceability from each exported slide back to its source data, so that I can revisit past content and show where every fact came from.

User story US-10: As the content operator, I want to manage reusable brand assets and carousel templates, and to have brand assets used only when they have actually been provided, so that the brand is applied consistently without placeholder or invented assets.
The platform provides a web interface for managing content projects: the user can create a project, list the existing projects and open a project.
When creating a content project, the user selects a competition, a season and a matchday. In the MVP the only selectable competition is the UEFA Champions League (seasons and phases: R-417).

For the selected competition, season and matchday, the Research Agent retrieves: the match results; the teams and scores of each match; the match dates; the competition standings; and relevant competition context.

relationships.target: ext:sports-data providers: a licensed sports-data API as preferred primary source and an independent official source for verification (PD-01, R-046), selected by the Architect (R-400) and authorized before any purchase or subscription (R-111)

records.statement: The user starts the research execution from the project and can follow its progress: the interface shows which workflow stage is pending, running, completed or failed, and a failed stage reports its reason.

Research results are stored as structured records. Each fact (for example a score, a match date or a standings row) carries its source attribution: the source it came from, a reference to its location in that source, and the retrieval time.

A Fact-Checking Agent independently verifies all factual information produced by research against reliable sources and records, for each fact, whether it is verified, the sources used and, when it is not verified, the reason. The verification rule is R-047 and R-048 (Product Owner decision PD-02) for scores, match dates and standings, and R-424 for other facts.

If a fact cannot be verified, publication approval is blocked for the content affected by that fact (every slide, headline, slide description or caption that uses it) until the fact is verified. Content that does not use the fact is not blocked.

The platform never invents scores, standings or match statistics. Every score, standing or match statistic that appears in generated content (slides, headlines, slide descriptions, captions) is taken from the verified data; content that contains such a value not present in the verified data is flagged and cannot be approved.
The platform clearly distinguishes verified facts from AI-generated commentary: each content element is identified as verified fact or generated commentary (presentation decided under R-404).
A Content Agent prepares, from the verified data: the carousel structure, the headlines, the slide descriptions, the social media captions and relevant hashtags.

relationships.target: ext:AI provider, to be selected by the Architect (R-401)

records.statement: A Graphic Design Agent creates the carousel slides: a cover slide, individual match-result slides (one per match), standings slides and a closing slide.
Slides are produced from reusable branded carousel templates; the same templates are reused across projects and matchdays.

Templates apply the El Deporte Rey GT identity: brand name El Deporte Rey GT, social handle @ElDeporteReyGT, mascot KETSI (images only when provided, R-034), and the colours purple, gold, blue and white.
The platform supports reusable brand assets: assets that have been provided (for example logos or mascot images) are registered once and reused by templates across projects.
Logos, team badges and mascot images are not assumed to exist; they are used only when they have been provided. Templates produce complete slides when such assets are absent.
Generated visuals preserve the exact verified scores and names: every score and name shown on a slide equals the verified value exactly (team names: the verified official names, R-052).

Numeric information is rendered deterministically: the same verified data and the same template always produce the same numeric text on the slide; numbers are never produced by a non-deterministic generation step.

A Visual QA Agent verifies every generated slide: scores and standings match the verified data; team names are correct; text fits the layout; visuals are consistent across the carousel; and the slide has the configured social media dimensions. Results are reported per slide and per check; failure handling is decided under R-420.
Before approving, the user can preview the generated carousel (all slides in carousel order) together with the captions and hashtags.
Explicit user approval is required before any content can be exported for publication; only approved assets can be exported (approval granularity: R-405; approval after a change: R-406).
The user can regenerate an individual slide without regenerating the other slides of the carousel.
The user can export approved assets for manual publication: the slide images and the captions with their hashtags.
The MVP does not publish automatically to any social platform; publication is done manually by the user from the exported files.
The platform keeps a history of generated content: past projects, with their generated slides, captions, approval state and exports, can be listed and reopened.
The platform maintains traceability from source data to exported slides: for every exported slide, the facts it shows, their verification status and their sources can be retrieved.

Facts are taken only from trustworthy, attributable data sources. The accepted sources are those set by Product Owner decision PD-01 (R-046): a licensed sports-data API as preferred primary source and an independent official source for verification.

Accepted data sources: research uses a licensed sports-data API as the preferred primary source, and fact-checking uses an independent official source for verification. Only accepted sources can make a fact verified (R-045). The providers that fill these roles are selected under R-400 and are not purchased or subscribed to without authorization (R-111).
A score, a match date or a standings value is verified only when two independent accepted sources (R-046) agree on it. A value reported by only one accepted source is not verified.

When accepted sources disagree on a fact, the fact is marked disputed and is not verified; the official competition publication is consulted (R-311); the fact is not marked verified until the discrepancy is resolved (R-423). Content that uses a disputed fact stays blocked (R-026), and the user cannot mark the fact verified manually (R-412).
Team names and the competition name appear in content as text. Slides use only existing brand assets that are authorized (R-309); no unauthorized logo, club badge or competition mark is used.

Templates reserve optional badge slots (for example one per team on a match-result slide). A badge slot shows an image only when an authorized badge asset exists for that team; until the Product Owner allows badges (R-413 option (b)) no badge is authorized, so the slots stay empty and the slides remain complete (R-034).

Each content project has a content language, which sets the language of the generated headlines, slide descriptions, captions and hashtags. The language is configurable per project; a new project uses Spanish unless the user selects another language (selectable languages: R-425).

Team names are preserved as verified official names: in every content language, every slide, headline, slide description and caption shows a team's name exactly as its verified official name, without translation, abbreviation or other change (source of the official name, hashtags and enforcement: R-426).
The MVP is local-first: the platform and its data run on the user's local machine (access to external providers: R-306).
MVP scope priorities, in order: (1) one competition, the UEFA Champions League; (2) matchday results and standings; (3) Instagram carousel generation; (4) manual approval and export.
The design supports future extension to additional competitions, additional social platforms and automated publishing; these extensions are not part of the MVP.
The technology stack is not prescribed by the Product Owner; the Architect proposes it based on these requirements.
Modular architecture with testable agent boundaries: each workflow stage (research, fact-checking, content, graphic design, visual QA) has defined inputs and outputs and can be tested in isolation.
Strong runtime validation: data received from providers and data exchanged between workflow stages is validated at run time against its expected structure; invalid data is rejected and not used.
Provider abstraction: AI providers and sports-data providers are configurable and can be replaced through configuration without changing the workflow stages.
Automated testing: the platform has automated tests covering the workflow stages and the business rules of this document.
Local development: the platform can be developed, run and tested on a local machine.
Avoid unnecessary infrastructure and premature complexity: the MVP introduces no component that the MVP scope (R-101) does not need.

During development, research and verification run on synthetic fixture data supplied through the provider abstraction (R-106), not on data from real sports-data providers; automated tests use synthetic fixtures only (R-225).
No service (a sports-data API, an AI provider or any other service) is purchased or subscribed to without authorization from the Product Owner.

The MVP is limited to team-level and competition-level data. No player-level information (for example player names, goal scorers, line-ups or player statistics) is collected, stored, generated or shown, and no personal data of users is kept (R-113).
The MVP has a single local operator and no login: the platform has no user accounts, no sign-in step and no user management.

Development services are bound to localhost only: the web interface and every other network service the platform starts listen only on the loopback interface and accept no connection from another machine (the web interface in MVP use as well, R-415 option (a)).

Processing of untrusted input inside the platform process (Product Owner decision PD-10). Within WI-1's scope (sports data from synthetic fixtures (R-110), the stub or a local AI provider, and operator-supplied PNG or JPEG brand files (R-033)), provider data, AI output and brand files may be parsed and decoded inside the platform process without thread or process isolation, provided these compensating controls are in place: allow-list schemas for provider data and AI output (R-105); size, dimension and timeout caps; file-signature checks on brand files; SVG files refused; no HTML parsing; inputs to slide rendering supplied as data URIs only; and an egress lint rule that confines network access. The acceptance is limited to this scope (R-116).

Condition of Product Owner decision PD-10: before the first real sports-data adapter, any hosted AI provider, or any new input type (for example SVG, HTML or web scraping, or archives) is introduced, a new security review is carried out and the Product Owner takes a new decision on the isolation of untrusted-input processing. Until then, R-115 does not cover them. Within WI-1 the condition holds when WI-1 delivers no real sports-data adapter, no hosted AI provider and no new input type; the security validation checks this (security design review control V-30).

Contract-evolution policy of the http-api contract (Product Owner decision PD-11). Within version v1 only additive changes are made: new optional request fields, new response fields, new operations and new problem codes. Removing an operation, a field or a problem code, or changing its meaning, is a breaking change; a breaking change needs a new major version path and a Product Owner decision. A new required request field or header is not an additive change.
Given the web interface is open, when the user creates a content project, then the project appears in the project list and, when opened, shows its competition, season and matchday.

The competition selector offers only the UEFA Champions League; the matchday selector lists only matchdays of the selected season; a project cannot be created until competition, season and matchday are all selected.

Given a fixture sports-data provider with a known matchday dataset, when research runs for that matchday, then the result contains every match of the matchday with both teams, the score of each finished match and its date, the full competition standings, and at least one competition-context item, each equal to the fixture values.

While research runs, the project view shows the status of each workflow stage; when the provider fails (simulated), the stage is shown as failed with a reason and the user can start the research again.
Every fact in a stored research result has a source, a source reference and a retrieval time; a fact without attribution is rejected by validation and is not stored as a research result.

After fact-checking, every fact has a verification status; a fact whose value differs between sources (a disagreement seeded in the fixture data) and that the official competition publication fixture does not settle is marked disputed and not verified, with a reason naming the sources.
Given one unverified score, approval of every slide, headline or caption that uses that score is refused with a message naming the fact, while content that does not use it can still be approved.
Given a stub AI provider that returns a caption (or a headline) containing a score not present in the verified data, that caption (or headline) is flagged and cannot be approved.
In the review view and in the stored content, every text element is identified as verified fact or generated commentary.

For a verified matchday dataset, the content draft contains an ordered carousel structure with a slide type for each slide, a headline and a description for each slide, a caption, and at least one hashtag.
The generated carousel contains a cover slide, one match-result slide for each match included in the carousel structure, at least one standings slide, and a closing slide.

Carousels generated for two different matchdays from the same templates use the same layouts and only colours from the configured brand palette (purple, gold, blue, white); a change to a template is applied to every carousel generated after the change.
With no logo, team badge or mascot image provided, a complete carousel is generated without errors and without any placeholder or substitute image for those assets.
Rendering the same slide twice from the same verified data and template produces identical numeric text; every score and team name placed on a slide equals the verified value exactly.

For each check (score or standing mismatch, incorrect team name, text overflow, inconsistent visual style, wrong dimensions), a slide seeded with that defect fails that check with a result naming it, and a correct slide passes all checks.
Before approval, the preview shows all slides in carousel order together with the caption and hashtags.
Export of content that has not been explicitly approved is refused; after explicit approval, the export succeeds.
Regenerating one slide changes only that slide and leaves the other slides unchanged; the regenerated slide goes through Visual QA again and needs approval again (R-406).
Export of an approved carousel produces one image file per approved slide, in carousel order and at the configured dimensions, and a text file containing the approved caption and hashtags.
The MVP has no function that publishes to a social platform, and no export step sends data to a social platform.
After an export, the project is listed in the history with its approval state and export time; reopening it shows the same slides and captions that were exported.
For any exported slide, the platform shows the facts displayed on it, their verification status and their sources.

Following the documented local setup, the full workflow (selection, research, fact-checking, content, design, visual QA, approval, export) runs on a single local machine, with external access only to the configured providers.
Replacing the configured AI provider and sports-data provider with stub providers requires only a configuration change, and the full workflow then runs end to end with the stubs.

Provider data or data passed between workflow stages that violates the expected structure (for example a missing score or a malformed date) is rejected with a validation error and is not used in any content.
Each workflow stage has automated tests that run it in isolation with fixture inputs; the automated test suite runs without access to real external providers.

The architecture review confirms that the competition, the target platform format (slide dimensions, maximum slides per carousel) and the publication mode are configuration or data, not logic fixed in the workflow stages.
Every fact in research and verification results names its source, and only sources accepted under PD-01 (R-046) can make a fact verified; a fact supported only by another source stays not verified.
A brand asset registered once is available to the templates of every later project without being provided again.

Given synthetic fixtures for a primary source and an independent verification source: a score, match date or standings value on which both agree is marked verified and cites both sources; a value present only in the primary source is not verified; a value supplied by a source that is not accepted does not count toward agreement.

Given a seeded disagreement between the two accepted sources on a score: the fact is marked disputed and not verified, the official competition publication fixture is consulted and the consultation is recorded, and content using the fact is blocked. When the official publication fixture agrees with one of the sources, the fact becomes verified with that value and its record shows the dispute and its resolution; when the official publication is unavailable or agrees with neither source, the fact stays disputed and not verified, and no user action can mark it verified.

A generated carousel shows team names and the competition name as text; its slides contain no club badge, competition logo or competition mark image and no image that is not an authorized registered brand asset; the templates contain the reserved badge slots, which stay empty while no authorized badge exists, and every slide is complete.

Given fixture provider data that includes player-level fields (for example goal scorers or line-ups), the stored research and verification results, the input passed to content drafting, the generated content and the exports contain no player-level field or value.
The architecture review confirms that the data model has no player entity or player-level attribute and no user-account entity.

With the platform started following the documented local setup, every listening network socket of the platform is bound to a loopback address; a connection to the web interface through the machine's non-loopback network address, or from another machine, is refused.
The web interface opens on the project list without a login step, and the platform offers no account creation, sign-in or user-management function.

A project created without choosing a language has content language Spanish, and the content stage drafts its headlines, slide descriptions, caption and hashtags in Spanish (with a stub AI provider: the stage receives Spanish as the language); a project set to another selectable language (R-425) is drafted in that language; two projects with different languages keep their own settings.

Given a fixture team whose verified official name contains accents or special characters, every slide, headline, slide description and caption generated for a Spanish project and for an English project shows the name exactly as verified; a slide seeded with a translated or abbreviated name fails the Visual QA team-name check, and a caption or headline using such a form is flagged and cannot be approved (R-426).
With the default configuration, every generated and exported slide is 1080 x 1350 pixels (portrait 4:5); Visual QA fails a slide of any other size.
The matchday selector offers only league-phase matchdays of the UEFA Champions League; knockout rounds cannot be selected.

Final carousel approval is refused while any included slide or the caption is not approved or is blocked; export is refused without the final approval; once every included slide and the caption are approved, the final approval and the export succeed.
In the development configuration and in the automated test suite, research and verification run end to end on synthetic fixture data, and no request is made to a real sports-data provider.

The architecture review confirms that the provider research covers, for each candidate provider, pricing, coverage, reliability and redistribution/licensing conditions; that development and automated testing need no purchased service or subscription; and that no service is purchased or subscribed to before the Product Owner authorizes it.

The MVP has one user role, the content operator of El Deporte Rey GT, who creates projects, runs research, reviews, approves and exports. The followers of @ElDeporteReyGT are the audience of the exported content, not users of the platform.
records.basis: Product Owner decision PD-05 (S-001 lines 29-30, R-415 option (a)) confirms a single local operator without login (R-113). That the followers are the audience and not platform users remains an assumption: S-000 refers only to 'the user' (lines 16 and 48) and names no other role.

records.statement: No logos, mascot images, team badges or brand fonts have been provided at the time of this analysis; the first templates are built without them.
records.basis: S-000 lines 81-82 say not to assume such assets exist unless provided; S-001 line 22 refers to existing authorized brand assets, but the intake inventory holds only the S-000 and S-001 texts and no asset files.

records.statement: The Research, Fact-Checking, Content, Graphic Design and Visual QA Agents of S-000 are functional stages of the product. Whether each stage uses an AI model, deterministic code or both is an architecture decision (for example, comparing rendered scores with verified data can be deterministic).
records.basis: S-000 lines 18-46 describe the responsibilities of each agent, not their implementation; lines 112-113 leave the technology to the Architect. These agents are product features, not framework roles.

records.statement: The only target social platform of the MVP is Instagram, so 'social media dimensions' (S-000 line 46) means the Instagram carousel format.
records.basis: S-000 line 104 prioritises Instagram carousel generation and lines 107-108 make other platforms a future extension.

records.statement: Export means saving the approved images and caption text as local files, which the user uploads to Instagram manually.
records.basis: S-000 lines 50 and 62 (export for manual publication), 95 (no automatic publishing) and 99 (local-first).

records.statement: 'Relevant competition context' (S-000 line 23) means short factual context about the matchday derived from competition data (for example the matchday number, the competition phase or positions in the standings); every factual claim in it is subject to fact-checking (R-025).
records.basis: S-000 line 23 does not define competition context; lines 25-26 require verification of all factual information.

records.statement: Local-first does not mean offline: the platform needs internet access at run time to reach the sports-data and AI providers.
records.basis: S-000 lines 18-26 and 87 require third-party data and line 123 configurable AI providers; line 99 sets where the platform runs, not that it is offline.

records.statement: No performance, availability or scale targets are set for the MVP; the expected load is that of a single operator.
records.basis: S-000 states no performance or scale target; line 99 (local-first MVP) and line 125 (avoid premature complexity).

records.statement: Research collects only the data items listed in S-000 lines 19-23; detailed match statistics (for example team-level possession or shots) are not collected in the MVP. Player-level data is excluded by Product Owner decision PD-04 (R-112).
records.basis: S-000 lines 18-23 list the research data; line 86 mentions match statistics only as something never to invent. PD-04 (S-001 lines 25-27) excludes player-level information but does not address team-level match statistics, so their exclusion stays an assumption.

records.statement: Authorized brand assets are the El Deporte Rey GT assets (for example a logo, KETSI images or brand fonts) that the Product Owner has provided for use. No club badge, competition logo or competition mark is authorized in the MVP; badges become usable only after a Product Owner decision allowing them (R-413 option (b)).
records.basis: S-001 lines 22-23 require existing authorized brand assets and forbid unauthorized logos, without saying how an asset is authorized; S-000 lines 81-82 tie the use of assets to their being provided; the adopted option (c) of R-413 keeps the badge slot empty until option (b) is decided.

records.statement: Fixed text in the templates (for example slide titles or labels on standings slides) follows the project's content language (R-051).
records.basis: S-001 line 34 makes the content language configurable per project; S-000 lines 28-33 list the generated content but not the fixed template text, so its language is not stated; a carousel in a single language is the consistent reading.

records.statement: The 'official competition publication' of S-001 line 18 is the competition organiser's official publication of results, match dates and standings for the UEFA Champions League, and it counts as an independent accepted source. It may be the same publication as the verification source of R-046; the Architect identifies it in the provider research (R-400).
records.basis: S-001 line 18 names the publication but not its publisher; S-001 lines 4-5 accept an independent official source for verification; the options of R-410 referred to the organiser's official publications.

records.statement: Which sports-data provider or providers does the platform use for research and verification?
records.resolution: Left to the Architect in the architecture stage, bounded by Product Owner decision PD-01 (S-001 lines 3-11): the Architect researches the available providers, their pricing, coverage, reliability and redistribution/licensing conditions, for a licensed sports-data API as preferred primary source and an independent official source for verification (R-046). The requirements stay provider-neutral (R-106); development and automated tests use synthetic fixtures (R-110); no service is purchased or subscribed to without the Product Owner's authorization (R-111).
records.recommendation: The Architect delivers the provider research with the architecture, with a proposed primary and verification source for the Product Owner's authorization.
records.basis: S-000 lines 112-113 (the Architect proposes the stack), 120 and 123 (provider abstraction, configurable sports-data providers); PD-01 (S-001 lines 3-11) sets the source roles and the research scope but names no provider.

records.statement: Which AI provider or providers and models do the AI-based workflow stages use?
records.resolution: Left to the Architect in the architecture stage, behind the provider abstraction (R-106). Automated tests use a deterministic stub provider. Provider credentials are never stored in the repository. No paid account, purchase or subscription is made without the Product Owner's authorization (R-111, PD-01).
records.recommendation: The Architect proposes a default provider and documents how to switch providers by configuration.
records.basis: S-000 lines 112-113, 120 and 123; S-000 names no AI provider; S-001 line 11 (no purchase or subscription without authorization).

records.statement: Which approach renders the slide images (for example programmatic template rendering, generative imagery, or a combination)?
records.resolution: Left to the Architect, bounded by R-035 and R-036: scores, standings, team names and all other numbers are placed on slides deterministically from the verified data; any generated imagery must not be the means by which those values appear on a slide.
records.recommendation: Template-based rendering for every fact-bearing element.
records.basis: S-000 lines 91-92 require deterministic numbers and exact names but name no rendering technique; lines 112-113 leave the stack to the Architect.

records.statement: Where and how are projects, research results, verification results, generated content and history stored?
records.resolution: Left to the Architect, bounded by R-100 (local-first), R-109 (no unnecessary infrastructure), R-043 (history) and R-044 (traceability).
records.recommendation: Local storage on the operator's machine with no separately hosted service.
records.basis: S-000 lines 99, 112-113 and 125; S-000 names no storage technology.

records.statement: Where and how is the distinction between verified facts and AI-generated commentary shown (review interface, stored data, exported images, captions)?
records.resolution: Recommended reversible default: every stored content element carries a provenance label (verified fact, with references to its facts, or generated commentary); the review view displays the label; exported images and captions carry no visible label; commentary must not state scores, standings or statistics that are not verified (R-027).
records.recommendation: Adopt the default as an Orchestrator decision; the Product Owner can ask for visible labels on exported content later.
records.basis: S-000 line 88 requires the distinction but not where it is shown; reversible, non-security default (autonomy.md MED-04).

records.statement: At what granularity is content approved: per slide, per caption, per carousel?
records.resolution: Confirmed by Product Owner decision PD-09 (S-001 line 44), which preserves the proposed default (Orchestrator decision OD-02): each slide and the caption have their own review state; a final carousel approval is possible only when every included slide and the caption are approved and none is blocked (R-026, R-420); export (R-041) requires the final carousel approval. Acceptance criterion: R-240.
records.basis: S-001 line 44 (preserve individual slide/caption approval and final approval); S-000 lines 48, 50, 60, 89-90 and 94.

records.statement: Does approval survive a later change, such as regenerating an approved slide or re-running research?
records.resolution: No. Approval applies to the exact version approved. Regenerating or otherwise changing an approved slide or caption, or re-running research, returns the changed content to pending review, re-runs Visual QA for changed slides and requires approval again.
records.basis: S-000 line 94 (explicit user approval before publication) and line 93 (traceability to exported slides): content changed after approval has not been explicitly approved.

records.statement: How does the carousel structure handle a matchday whose individual match-result slides, plus cover, standings and closing slides, exceed the maximum number of slides Instagram allows in one carousel post?
records.resolution: Recommended reversible default: the maximum number of slides per carousel is a configuration value, set to the limit Instagram publishes at implementation time; when the structure exceeds it, the Content Agent splits the matchday into numbered carousels within the same project, each with its own cover and closing slide; the user can exclude matches from a carousel. Individual match-result slides (S-000 line 36) are kept.
records.recommendation: Adopt the default as an Orchestrator decision.
records.basis: S-000 lines 36, 46 and 104 require individual match slides and correct social media dimensions but set no slide count; reversible, non-security default (autonomy.md MED-04).

records.statement: Which slide dimensions does the Instagram carousel use?
records.resolution: Confirmed by Product Owner decision PD-09 (S-001 line 43), which preserves the proposed format (Orchestrator decision OD-04): portrait 4:5 at 1080 x 1350 pixels, held as configuration and confirmed against Instagram's published specifications at implementation time; Visual QA checks the configured value. Acceptance criterion: R-238.
records.basis: S-001 line 43 (preserve the proposed 1080x1350 carousel format); S-000 lines 46 and 104.

records.statement: How are matches that are not finished, postponed or abandoned, and matchdays still in progress, handled?
records.resolution: Recommended reversible default: only matches with a verified final result get a match-result slide; matches without one are listed in the project with their verified status (for example scheduled or postponed) and are left out of the carousel; standings slides show the verified date and time the standings refer to; research on a matchday with no finished match reports that no result content can be produced.
records.recommendation: Adopt the default as an Orchestrator decision.
records.basis: S-000 lines 86 and 89-90 (no invented results; block unverified content) do not cover incomplete matchdays; reversible, consistent with those rules (autonomy.md MED-04).

records.statement: Which sports-data sources may the platform use, and does the Product Owner accept their licensing and terms of use, including use of the data in content published on a public social account? Options: (a) a licensed commercial sports-data API whose terms allow derived social media content; (b) free or public sources, such as the competition organiser's official publications, after the Product Owner confirms their terms allow this use; (c) a combination: one licensed API as primary source and an official public source as the independent verification source.
records.resolution: Decided by the Product Owner: PD-01, option (c) (S-001 lines 3-11). A licensed sports-data API is the preferred primary source and an independent official source is used for verification (R-045, R-046). The Architect researches available providers, pricing, coverage, reliability and redistribution/licensing conditions (R-400); synthetic fixtures are used during development (R-110); no service is purchased or subscribed to without authorization (R-111). Acceptance of a specific provider's terms follows the Architect's research. This document gives no legal assessment of any provider's terms.
records.recommendation: Option (c) had been recommended; the decision adopts it.
records.basis: Product Owner decision record S-001 lines 3-11 (precedence level 1), decision ID PD-01.

records.statement: When is a fact 'verified'? S-000 requires independent verification against reliable sources but does not define the rule. Options: (a) two independent sources accepted under R-410 agree exactly on the value; any disagreement, or only one available source, means not verified; (b) the competition organiser's official publication alone suffices; other sources are used only when it is unavailable; (c) the research source and one independent source must agree, and when they disagree the organiser's official publication decides.
records.resolution: Decided by the Product Owner: PD-02, option (a) (S-001 lines 13-19). Scores, match dates and standings are verified only when two independent accepted sources agree (R-047). If sources disagree, the official competition publication is consulted, and a disputed fact is not marked verified until the discrepancy is resolved (R-048, R-423). The procedure stated in S-001 lines 17-19 takes precedence over the option (a) wording above, which left a disagreement unverified without further consultation. Facts other than scores, match dates and standings: R-424.
records.recommendation: Option (a) had been recommended; the decision adopts it with the disagreement procedure of S-001 lines 17-19.
records.basis: Product Owner decision record S-001 lines 13-19 (precedence level 1), decision ID PD-02.

records.statement: Can the user override the block on unverified content, for example by marking a fact as verified manually?
records.resolution: No. In the MVP an unverified fact keeps the affected content blocked; the user can re-run research and verification, or remove the affected content from the carousel. Adding an override would be a scope change for the Product Owner.
records.basis: S-000 lines 86 and 89-90 require blocking publication approval for affected content and name no exception.

records.statement: May slides use club badges and competition names or marks (for example the UEFA Champions League name and logo), and in what form may team names appear? Options: (a) team names and the competition name as plain text, and only El Deporte Rey GT assets; no club badges and no competition logos or marks; (b) badges and competition marks are used when the Product Owner provides the files and confirms the right to use them; (c) as (a) for the MVP, with an optional badge slot in templates that stays empty until (b) is decided.
records.resolution: Decided by the Product Owner: PD-03, option (c) (S-001 lines 21-23). Team names (and the competition name) appear as text; only existing authorized brand assets are used; optional badge slots are reserved; no unauthorized logos are used (R-049, R-050, R-309). Option (b) remains a possible later Product Owner decision. No legal assessment of trademark use is given here.
records.recommendation: Option (c) had been recommended; the decision adopts it.
records.basis: Product Owner decision record S-001 lines 21-23 (precedence level 1), decision ID PD-03.

records.statement: Does the MVP process personal data? S-000 lists team-level data (results, scores, dates, standings, competition context) and mentions neither player data nor user accounts. Options: (a) team- and competition-level data only: no player-level data (for example goal scorers) and no personal data of users; (b) include public player data such as goal scorers' names on slides and in captions; (c) as (b), plus player statistics.
records.resolution: Decided by the Product Owner: PD-04, option (a) (S-001 lines 25-27). The initial MVP is limited to team-level and competition-level data and introduces no player-level information (R-112); with no user accounts (PD-05, R-113) no personal data of users is kept. Recording this in the project configuration's risk profile is a configuration task, not a requirement.
records.recommendation: Option (a) had been recommended; the decision adopts it.
records.basis: Product Owner decision record S-001 lines 25-27 (precedence level 1), decision ID PD-04.

records.statement: What is the user and authentication model of the MVP? S-000 refers only to 'the user' and asks for a local-first MVP. Options: (a) a single local operator without login; the web interface accepts connections from the local machine only; (b) a local login with a password for one or more operators; (c) multi-user accounts with roles, which implies hosting outside the local-first MVP.
records.resolution: Decided by the Product Owner: PD-05, option (a) (S-001 lines 29-31). A single local operator without login (R-113); development services are bound to localhost only, and the web interface accepts connections from the local machine only (R-114). Hosting, remote access or several operators would need a new Product Owner decision.
records.recommendation: Option (a) had been recommended; the decision adopts it.
records.basis: Product Owner decision record S-001 lines 29-31 (precedence level 1), decision ID PD-05.

records.statement: In which language is content generated (headlines, slide descriptions, captions, hashtags), and how are team names displayed? Language options: (a) Spanish; (b) English; (c) configurable per project. Team-name options: (i) exactly as in the verified data; (ii) a Product Owner-approved display name per team (for example a Spanish name), bound to the verified team identity and checked by Visual QA.
records.resolution: Decided by the Product Owner: PD-06 (S-001 lines 33-35). Language: option (c), configurable per project with Spanish as the default (R-051; selectable languages R-425). Team names: option (i), verified official names are preserved (R-052; official-name source and enforcement R-426).
records.recommendation: Language (c) with Spanish as default and names (i) had been recommended; the decision adopts them.
records.basis: Product Owner decision record S-001 lines 33-35 (precedence level 1), decision ID PD-06.

records.statement: Which UEFA Champions League seasons and competition phases are in MVP scope?
records.resolution: Phases: league-phase matchdays only for the initial MVP, confirmed by Product Owner decision PD-09 (S-001 line 45), which preserves the proposed scope (Orchestrator decision OD-06); knockout rounds, which have no standings table, are a later extension; seasons played under a different competition format are outside the MVP. Seasons: S-001 does not address them, so the reversible default of OD-06 stays in force (seasons covered by the accepted data source, starting with the current season). Acceptance criterion: R-239.
records.basis: S-001 line 45 (preserve league-phase-only scope for the initial MVP); S-000 lines 12 and 102-103; the season part rests on Orchestrator decision OD-06 (autonomy.md MED-04).

records.statement: What are the exact brand colour values and fonts?
records.resolution: Recommended reversible default: provisional values for purple, gold, blue and white and a provisional font are held as brand configuration and used until the Product Owner supplies official values; no logo or mascot image is created as a substitute (R-034).
records.recommendation: Adopt the default; ask the Product Owner for official values in the next status report.
records.basis: S-000 lines 73-77 name the colours but not their values, and name no font; reversible, non-security default (autonomy.md MED-04).

records.statement: How long is the content history kept, and can it be deleted?
records.resolution: Recommended reversible default: all projects and their versions are kept locally without automatic expiry; the MVP offers no deletion function (deleting user data is a destructive operation, autonomy.md HIGH-02).
records.recommendation: Adopt the default as an Orchestrator decision.
records.basis: S-000 line 63 asks for a history and is silent on retention and deletion; additive and reversible (autonomy.md MED-04).

records.statement: What happens when a Visual QA check fails?
records.resolution: Recommended default: a failure of the score, standing, team-name, text-fit or dimension checks blocks approval of that slide until a regenerated version passes (data mismatches are already blocking under R-026 and R-035); a visual-consistency finding is shown as a warning that the user must acknowledge before approving.
records.recommendation: Adopt the default as an Orchestrator decision.
records.basis: S-000 lines 41-46 list the checks but not the handling of failures; lines 89-92 already make data mismatches blocking; reversible (autonomy.md MED-04).

records.statement: Which file formats and file naming does the export use?
records.resolution: Implementation choice within R-041 and R-218: an image format accepted by Instagram (lossless preferred for sharp text), file names in carousel order, captions and hashtags as UTF-8 text.
records.recommendation: Left to the implementing agent.
records.basis: S-000 lines 50 and 62 require export of images and captions without naming formats.

records.statement: Are captions, headlines and slide descriptions, which the Visual QA Agent does not check, also subject to the rule against invented facts?
records.resolution: Yes. R-027 applies to all generated content, including captions, headlines and slide descriptions.
records.basis: S-000 line 86 (never invent scores, standings or match statistics) and lines 89-90 apply to all content, not only to slides.

records.statement: When is a disputed fact (R-048) resolved, so that it can be marked verified?
records.resolution: Applying PD-02 (S-001 lines 13-19) as a whole: a disputed fact is resolved when a single value is supported by two independent accepted sources, for example when the official competition publication (R-311) agrees with one of the disagreeing sources, or when a later retrieval shows the sources in agreement. The verification stage records the disagreeing values, the consultation and the outcome. If the official publication is unavailable, gives no value, gives a third value, or is the same source as one of the disagreeing ones, no value has two independent accepted sources, so the fact stays disputed and not verified and the affected content stays blocked (R-026). The user can re-run verification but cannot set the value or mark the fact verified manually (R-412).
records.basis: S-001 lines 14-15 (agreement of two independent accepted sources is required) and 17-19 (consult the official competition publication; disputed facts are not verified until the discrepancy is resolved); S-000 lines 89-90; R-412.

records.statement: Which verification rule applies to facts other than scores, match dates and standings (for example which teams played a match, a match status such as postponed, or competition context)?
records.resolution: Recommended reversible default: the PD-02 rule (R-047, R-048, R-423) applies to every fact used in content, which is the strictest reading of S-000 lines 25-26 ('independently verifies all factual information'). Generated commentary that states no fact is not subject to verification (R-028, R-404).
records.recommendation: Adopt the default as an Orchestrator decision; the Product Owner can relax it later for specific fact types.
records.basis: S-001 lines 13-15 name only scores, match dates and standings; S-000 lines 25-26 require independent verification of all factual information; the default is stricter, consistent with PD-02 and reversible (autonomy.md MED-04).

records.statement: Which content languages can be selected for a project?
records.resolution: Recommended reversible default: Spanish (the default) and English, the two languages named in the options the Product Owner decided on (R-416); the list of selectable languages is configuration, so adding a language needs no change to the workflow stages.
records.recommendation: Adopt the default as an Orchestrator decision.
records.basis: S-001 line 34 (option (c), configurable per project, Spanish by default) does not list the selectable languages; R-416 options (a) and (b); reversible (autonomy.md MED-04).

records.statement: Which name is a team's 'verified official name', how are differing name forms across sources handled, and what happens when generated text uses another form?
records.resolution: Recommended reversible default: (1) the official name is the team name as given by the independent official source of R-046; (2) the team identity (which team a name refers to) is verified under R-424 by matching the team across the accepted sources, a data-matching design task for the Architect; a team that cannot be matched stays not verified and blocks the content that uses it (R-026); (3) the official name is shown exactly in every content language (R-052): a slide with another form fails the Visual QA team-name check (R-420), and a generated headline, slide description or caption with another form is flagged and cannot be approved until corrected or regenerated, as for invented values (R-027); (4) hashtags are not name displays and may use a hashtag-safe form of the official name (without spaces or punctuation).
records.recommendation: Adopt the default as an Orchestrator decision; if the Orchestrator judges point (1) or (4) to be business-rule semantics, confirm them with the Product Owner in the next status report.
records.basis: S-001 line 35 (preserve verified official names) and lines 4-5 (independent official source) do not say which source supplies the official name, how name forms of different sources are matched, or how a violation is handled; S-000 lines 43 and 92; consistent with R-027 and R-420; reversible (autonomy.md MED-04).

records.statement: May untrusted input (provider data, AI output and operator-supplied brand image files) be parsed and decoded inside the platform process without isolation, or must its processing be isolated (escalation E-07, architecture issue U-03)? Options: (A) accept in-process processing for WI-1's scope (synthetic fixtures, stub or local AI, operator-supplied PNG or JPEG brand files) with compensating controls, on the condition that the first real sports-data adapter, any hosted AI provider or any new input type needs a new security review and a new Product Owner decision on isolation; (B) isolate image decoding and AI-response parsing in a worker thread with resource limits and a deadline; (C) isolate them in a separate process with file-system access limited to the input.
records.resolution: Decided by the Product Owner: PD-10, option (A) (S-002 line 1, 'E-07 A'). In-process processing of untrusted input is accepted for WI-1's scope with the compensating controls of option (A) (R-115). The first real sports-data adapter, any hosted AI provider or any new input type (SVG, HTML or web scraping, archives) needs a new security review and a new Product Owner decision on isolation (R-116). Options (B) and (C) are not adopted.
records.recommendation: Option (A) had been recommended by the architect and the security reviewer; the decision adopts it.
records.basis: Product Owner decision record S-002 line 1 (precedence level 1), decision ID PD-10, answering escalation E-07. The option texts are those presented to the Product Owner in docs/work-items/WI-1/security/design-review.md section 5 'Q2 and U-03' (options table), which classifies the question under autonomy.md HIGH-03 (isolation of untrusted-input processing); see also docs/work-items/WI-1/architecture/architecture-delta.md section 8, U-03.

records.statement: Which contract-evolution policy governs the http-api contract (escalation E-08, architecture issue U-04)? Proposed policy: within v1 only additive changes (new optional request fields, new response fields, new operations, new problem codes); removing or changing the meaning of an operation, field or code is a breaking change that needs a new major version path and a Product Owner decision.
records.resolution: Decided by the Product Owner: PD-11 (S-002 line 1, 'E-08 approve as written with your recommendations'). The policy is approved as written (R-117). That every change to the declared contract also gets a Contract Safety assessment is framework process, not a product requirement.
records.recommendation: The policy as written had been recommended by the architect and found without security objection by the security reviewer; the decision adopts it.
records.basis: Product Owner decision record S-002 line 1 (precedence level 1), decision ID PD-11, answering escalation E-08 (raised under autonomy.md HIGH-06, contract-evolution policy). The policy text is that of docs/work-items/WI-1/architecture/architecture-delta.md section 2.1, 'Versioning and compatibility' (recommendation in section 8, U-04); docs/work-items/WI-1/security/design-review.md section 6 (no security objection) and section 5 Q1 (a newly required header is not additive under this policy).

candidateResolutions.reason: S-001 line 61 ('Do not merge into main, push or deploy.') is a process direction to the framework, not a product requirement. It is listed in flaggedInstructions with action not-acted-on; it matches existing framework policy (autonomy.md HIGH-08; policy.authorizations all false), so it changes no policy, gate, precedence level or file ownership.

flaggedInstructions.text: Use the installed ORCH-V3 framework. Start with requirements analysis and normalization. Generate: Product requirements. User stories. Acceptance criteria. Architecture considerations. Dependencies. Risks. Proposed MVP delivery phases.
Resolve routine technical decisions autonomously within established project policies.
Do not begin implementation during this analysis phase.
Enable the frontend-developer role in the project configuration through the authorized configuration workflow.

Execution: 1. Record all six Product Owner decisions. 2. Have the Product Manager update the requirements. 3. Verify traceability and acceptance criteria. 4. Update project configuration through the authorized workflow. 5. Run orch requirements check, tracker check and validate. 6. Commit the approved requirements changes to the work branch. 7. Report readiness for /orchestrate:plan WI-1.
Do not implement application features yet.
Do not merge into main, push or deploy.

workItems.title: Phase 1: Foundation - local web interface for a single operator without login and bound to localhost, content projects and UEFA Champions League league-phase selection, provider abstraction with synthetic fixture and stub providers, runtime validation, automated test harness (Initial Scope priority 1)
Phase 2: Verified matchday results and standings - research, source attribution, two-source fact-checking with the dispute procedure, team- and competition-level data only (Initial Scope priority 2)

Phase 3: Instagram carousel generation - content drafting in the project language, branded templates with badge slots and authorized assets, deterministic slide rendering at 1080 x 1350, visual QA (Initial Scope priority 3)
Phase 4: Review, per-slide and caption approval with final approval, manual export, history and traceability (Initial Scope priority 4)
